newsitem.title: USA: Albright wants U.S. aid to Israel at current level.
newsitem.headline: Albright wants U.S. aid to Israel at current level.

text.p: Maintaining U.S. aid to Israel at $3 billion a year is critical as the Jewish state moves forward in the peace process, Secretary of State-designate Madeleine Albright said Monday.
In written answers to more than 200 questions posed as part of her Senate confirmation process, Albright replied "yes" when asked if aid to Israel should be kept at current levels.

This assistance is "a concrete demonstration of the U.S. pledge to sustain and enhance Israel's security and well-being ...(and) will remain critical as Israel moves forward in the peace process," Albright said.

Outgoing Secretary of State Warren Christopher, whose resignation was effective Monday, last week raised the possibility in his farewell speech that aid to Israel and Egypt could be jeopardized if Congress does not increase foreign affairs spending.

But it would be politically difficult to try to do so now, in part because of the enormous support for Israel among American Jews but also because Israel's right-wing government has just concluded a long-delayed pact with the Palestinians on Hebron that keeps the peace process alive.

The Senate Foreign Relations Committee Monday voted unanimously to recommend that the full Senate confirm Albright as the first woman secretary of state. The full Senate is expected to act on Wednesday.
